title: Writing a brand story people can repeat
excerpt: If your own team can’t retell it in a sentence, your customers never will.
body:
A brand story isn’t a founder biography, or a mission statement with the nouns changed. It’s a short, true account of why the brand exists and what it believes, written so other people can carry it for you.

We test every story with a simple exercise: ask five people in the business to say it out loud, without notes. If five different versions come back, the story isn’t finished. The version that survives retelling is usually the shortest one.

Good stories have tension in them: something that was wrong, and a decision to put it right. “Tea was sold in a hurry, so we made one worth waiting for.” That single line is a position, a point of view and a design brief.

Write for the person repeating the story, not the person reading it. Plain words travel further than clever ones.
